newsitem.title: CHINA: China to join WTO soon - Italian PM says.
newsitem.headline: China to join WTO soon - Italian PM says.

text.p: Visiting Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday he expected China to join the World Trade Organisation (WTO) soon and that Italy backed Beijing's long-delayed bid to enter the global body.
Prodi said it was difficult to give an exact date for China's entry into the WTO, but said he expected the admission "very soon".
"It's difficult to have a World Trade Organisation without China," Prodi told a news conference in Beijing.
Market access was holding up China's application, he said without elaborating.
In May, Chinese Assistant Foreign Trade Minister Long Yongtu pledged to return to the next round of WTO entry talks in Geneva in July with better offers on market access.
China applied to join the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, the WTO's predecessor, in 1986, but progress has been slow.
WTO chief Renato Ruggiero urged China in May to make a very ambitious market-access offer, a major issue in service and farm sectors.

Beijing's decade-long bid to join the WTO has also been held up because it wants to join on the terms accorded to developing countries, which are considered to be easier. This would allow Beijing more time to adjust its trade practices to the WTO's internationally agreed upon rules for global free trade.
Some Western nations, including the United States, insist that China's economy is too big to be afforded developing country treatment.
Prodi said Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro was expected to visit China in early 1997.
